findings.title: Overwrite docs promise a never exception the type does not implement
findings.why_it_matters: The comments say TType is retained when TWith is never, but both conditional branches distribute over TWith and therefore evaluate to never in that case. This leaves the published internal type contract inconsistent with its behavior. The PR's main primitive-with-middleware regression is fixed, but this edge case remains ambiguous relative to the earlier suggestion to preserve a non-never type.
evidence: packages/server/src/core/internals/utils.ts:21-24: the non-object TWith branch is conditional on TWith extends any; a never TWith distributes to never.
packages/server/src/core/internals/utils.ts:25-30: the other TType branch also uses TWith extends any, so a never TWith likewise produces never.
findings.suggested_fix: Align the comment and chosen contract: remove the never exception if never should replace TType, or add an explicit [TWith] extends [never] case if the previous type should be retained.

residual_risks: The unresolved reviewer request for keywise overwrite when both inputs are objects and full TWith replacement otherwise is implemented by the current conditional type. The regression test verifies string input inference with middleware and string output inference.
testing_gaps: The added test does not assert the never-TWith behavior described by the new type documentation, nor does it assert the voidWithMiddleware router entry declared in the same file.
